newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end well down on Wall Street jitters.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end well down on Wall Street jitters.

text.p: * New Zealand shares soften as Dow tumbles
* Local market seen toppy and jittery about U.S. direction
* Domestic interest rates an inhibiter
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
335 -1 * NZSC cap index -37.10 at 5,148.77
360 -3 * Volume NZ$52.4 million. Futures -5, 1212
751 -1 * Other movers - +5 -20
New Zealand's share market closed 0.7 percent lower on Friday as jitters from Wall Street fed through to the local market.
The top 40 index ended 17.53 down at 2400.27 on volume of $52.4 million.
Brokers said the Dow's 94 point slide was the main reason for the slide but the turn up in local interest rates also weighed on equities.
Brokers said the market will be nervous how Wall Street behaves tonight. And the local market appeared overbought.
"It (the New Zealand market) looks a little toppy and I wouldn't be surprised if it drifts a little lower," said JB Were's Luke Koekoek.
The sharp fall in paper stocks in the U.S. overnight told on the local market as well.
Fletcher Paper fell three cents to $2.86 and Carter Holt one cent to $3.35.
Brierley Investments took a sharp three cent fall despite its British hotel group Thistle performing at a post-float high.

Holding the market together was a relatively firm performance from Telecom. It ended just one cent off at $7.51 despite broker NatWest cutting its recommendation on Telecom to underperfomer from hold.
There was active two-way business in Lion Nathan which fell three cents to $3.60.
